div.head: ECf 32 A 5
div.ab: Statutum est enim, quod ibi debent populi omnes et gentes uniuerse singulis annis, semel in anno scilicet, conuenire, scilicet in capite kalendarum Maii, et se fide et sacramento non fracto ibi in unum et insimul confederare et consolidare sicut coniurati fratres ad defendendum regnum contra alienigenas et contra inimicos, una cum domino suo rege, et terras et honores illius omni fidelitate cum eo seruare, et quod illi ut domino suo regi intra et extra regnum uniuersum Britannie fideles esse uolunt.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 655 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann’s letter a after “Maii” is his upright a (Erklärungen).

note.seg: ähnlich ebd. 2. 9. Der Treu- und Friedenseid, in der Grafschaft 1166, 1181, 1195, 1199, 1205 neu verordnet, kommt auch im Londoner Folcesmot vor
similarly ibid. 2. 9. The oath of fealty and peace, newly ordained in the shire in 1166, 1181, 1195, 1199, 1205, also occurs in the London folkmoot
entnommen wohl technischer Rechtssprache, in der es ungestabten Eid bedeutet; der Londoner meint aber unverbrüchlich
probably taken from technical legal language, in which it means an oath not sworn with the staff; but the Londoner means unbreakable
nicht Eidbrüder, sondern geschworene Volksgenossen, auch u. 32 C 1; vgl. o. S. 490n
not sworn brothers, but sworn fellow-countrymen, also below 32 C 1; cf. above, p. 490, note n

div.ab: For it is decreed that all the peoples and all the nations must come together there every year, namely once a year, that is, at the head of the Kalends of May, and there bind and unite themselves together and as one by faith and unbroken oath, like sworn brothers, to defend the kingdom against foreigners and against enemies, together with their lord the king, and to preserve his lands and honours with him in all fidelity, and that they will be faithful to him as their lord king within and without the whole kingdom of Britain.

note.seg: Gemeint ist eine Volksversammlung aller Stämme Britanniens (s. d. Gl 4); doch ist der Traum deutlich von Londoner Kommunalzuständen allein eingegeben, laut der Namen des folces-imot und der motbelle, sowie der gegenseitigen Verbrüderung. Vgl. Gl Königstreue 7g; Eidbrüder 6. Verf. scheint unter fremden Volksfeinden in England um 1195—1205 zu verstehen die Französ. Adligen, Prälaten und Soldtruppen des Königs. — Mit Unrecht gilt diese Fabel vom Maifeld als Wirklichkeit bei Ducange s. v. Campus Martii. — o. p.18 Rs

What is meant is a popular assembly of all the peoples of Britain (see that word in Gl 4); but the dream is clearly inspired by London communal conditions alone, judging by the names folces-imot and motbelle, and the mutual sworn brotherhood. Cf. Gl Königstreue 7g; Eidbrüder 6. By foreign enemies of the people in England about 1195—1205 the author seems to mean the king's French nobles, prelates and mercenaries. — This fable of the May-field is wrongly taken as reality by Ducange s. v. Campus Martii. — o. p.18 Rs
